transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Alex, Dana, Marcus, Sofia, Ben (OliveBridge)

Summary:
Jordan: quick renewal check-in, readout from the on-prem feasibility, align next steps for pilot billing and SOW.

00:00 Jordan: alright everyone thanks for carving time today, um this is Jordan from Redwood, joined by Priya our solutions engineer. we wanted to run through the readout from the past two weeks, confirm the renewal window and line up the on-prem pilot in eu, and make sure security asks are mapped.
00:18 Alex: thanks, yeah uh we've been waiting on the definitive cost for the eu on-prem pilot and wanted to make sure the SLA and audit capabilities line up with our compliance needs, also timeline — procurement wants to lock something before end of month.
00:32 Priya: great, quick orientation — the pilot we're proposing is a minimal cluster in your eu datacenter (customer-managed), a private control-plane with Redwood Private v1 — sorry, the transcription sometimes shows 'Redwood Private' as 'Redwood pri-mate' — but basically turnkey control plane, we ship a containerized runtime and orchestration bits.
00:50 Dana: can you clarify the infra footprint? like how many GPUs, what g4/gbx. we are leaning toward A100 equivalent.
01:05 Priya: yes, for the models you're running (70B family) our recommendation for a realistic latency SLO is 4x A100 p4d equivalents. For the pilot I'd recommend 4 GPUs for functional workloads and then a reserved uplift if you want production traffic, pricing differs if you want reserved capacity vs burst.
01:28 Ben: on that, what's the difference in billing if we go reserved vs on-demand? last time we saw something from NebulaCloud that looked cheaper but lacked audit logs.
01:40 Jordan: reserved (Dedicated) is commit-based monthly/annual and gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost; on-demand for a private deployment still has per-token/usage overlay if you choose burst. We'll put the numbers in the quote — high level: reserved ~30-40% cheaper at our mid-tier GPU profiles.
01:59 Sofia: security — we need KMS integration, HSM option, and specific audit log retention to 7 years for some workflows. can you support HSM-backed keys and exportable audit logs?
02:14 Priya: yes, Private supports customer KMS or HSM integration, though there are some network constraints for key wrapping. logs are exportable, we can ship periodic offload to your SIEM. small caveat: the out-of-the-box retention is shorter, long-term retention costs extra.
02:37 Alex: also curious about model fallback — if the full 70B spikes cost, can we route to a quantized 13B variant automatically? how much work is that?
02:50 Priya: we have routing policies — you can set latency-first or cost-first and fallback to a compatible model variant. engineering side, it's mostly mapping model versions and acceptable quality deltas. Primary work is validating your prompt evaluation set to ensure 13B meets quality.
03:10 Marcus: procurement angle — we need a pilot SOW that includes termination clauses and an explicit renewal cadence. preferred payment terms net45.
03:20 Jordan: understood, we'll prepare draft SOW with pilot objectives, termination rights, and renewal window aligned to your fiscal close.
03:30 [short crosstalk] Marcus: also need an SLA table for the pilot, even if limited.
03:36 Priya: we can provide a pilot-level table — best-effort vs production SLA.
03:42 Jordan: ok quick readout of the on-prem feasibility work: Ben and Dana's team validated network egress costs, we saw a small NAT translation issue to the control plane which Priya's team has a workaround for. Priya, can you summarize the perf numbers?
03:57 Priya: sure. We ran a micro-benchmark with 8k token sequences for internal tests, observed tail latency variance with KV cache warmup. Median p95 tokens/sec matched our predictions, but cold-starts had up to 1.4x slower latency. As we suspected, prefix caching reduced repeated token cost by about 30%. note: the transcription may say 'KV cache' as 'k-v cat' occasionally.
04:28 Alex: that matches our data shape — many long-context calls with repeated prefixes. do you have recommendations on config?
04:36 Priya: enable persistent KV cache across sessions and set batching windows aggressively for low-latency traffic; for very low latency use dedicated p4d topology and smaller batch sizes. we'll include recommended config in the benchmark plan.
04:50 Ben: what about failover — if eu nodes are saturated do you support cross-region fallback to hosted in eu-west-1 or do we keep everything local due to data residency?
05:02 Jordan: fallback is configurable — you can allow model-level fallbacks to hosted/managed instances in the eu region, but if strict residency is required we can limit fallbacks. that's a policy decision on your side.
05:14 Sofia: on compliance — we need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC. plus exportable audit trails per token for certain endpoints. can you scope token-level audit logs?
05:26 Priya: we can produce token-level traces for flagged routes; note there are PII implications so we'll need to coordinate redaction rules. For SAML/SSO yes, enterprise SSO is supported and RBAC maps to your identity provider groups.
05:40 Alex: is the SOC2 package the same for Private as Hosted? we need to be sure about the differences.
05:46 Jordan: Private customers get broadened artifacts but some infra controls are customer-managed; we'll share a SOC2 addendum and gap list showing what's our responsibility vs yours.
05:56 Dana: timeline — we can sign pilot SOW if RedWood provides pricing by next week. procurement needs line items broken out: pilot, reserved uplift, add-on logs retention, benchmarks.
06:08 Jordan: that's doable. action items: Priya will send the perf plan and test harness, Jordan will send updated quote and SOW draft, Sofia will send security checklist.
06:18 Marcus: one more thing — cost caps, if usage exceeds pilot we want auto-alerts and a hard stop, not soft.
06:26 Priya: we support budget hooks and hard caps at route/token level, we'll include example config.
06:33 Alex: ok good. any blockers known from your side?
06:36 Priya: just the KMS network path and one kernel mismatch for our quantized model — but we have a mitigation: ephemeral local key wrapping via your HSM and a kernel shim that avoids the mismatch at the cost of a small perf hit. we'll document that in the plan.
06:58 Jordan: let's recap next steps: send pricing (Jordan) by 7/15, perf plan (Priya) by 7/13, customer docs (OliveBridge) on network/KMS by 7/14, schedule the pilot run for 7/17.
07:12 Alex: sounds good. we'll prioritize procurment but might need net60 for invoices — Marcus will flag.
07:20 Marcus: yep i'll follow up to get internal approve.
07:26 Sofia: also please include a sample audit export schema.
07:30 Priya: will do.
07:32 [wrap-up] Jordan: cool thank you all, we'll circulate the notes and action items. if folks want a deeper technical deep dive on the kernel shim and quantization tradeoffs we can block time next week.
07:45 Ben: thanks.
07:47 End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swap (Redwood product names, 'KV cache' mis-typed), small overlaps and filler words preserved.

Referenced artifacts (links provided in chat):
- draft SOW template (link shared by Jordan)
- perf test harness repo (Priya: github.com/redwood/perf-harness - link in chat)
- SOC2 addendum and security checklist (Jordan: redwood.com/security/soc2-addendum - link in chat)

Pilot acceptance criteria (captured during call):
- Successful run of 1 hour steady-state at expected QPS with pkts < target p95 latency
- KV cache persistence reduces repeated prefix cost by >=20%
- Audit log export and SSO/RBAC validated in staging
- Agreement on reserved uplift price or documented fallback policy
